correctness.rationale: For any m,n≥2 and individually distinct marked colors, the pointwise automorphism stabilizer is row/column permutation on unmarked coordinate values and, only for square boards with a matching of marks, optional coordinate transpose. If two marks share a row, Row(r)={e,f}∪(N(e)∩N(f)), visibly a union of first-round cells; marked columns/remaining marked rows become unions by second round. If marks are nonattacking, first-round marked-adjacency signatures give unordered occupied coordinate types; for m≠n the orientation ambiguity is separated by respective neighbor counts n−t and m−t (or minus one) at second round. Equality of color classes to orbits follows from equivariance and the recovered coordinate signatures. Counts are (a+1_{a<m})(b+1_{b<n}) generally and t(t+1)/2+(t+1)1_{t<m} for square matching; witness of a second strict round is verified. Independent recomputation of all marked subsets on 2x3,3x3,3x4 boards checked equality of partitions and class counts; these finite examples supplement the all-size argument.
